title: Circuit breaker: fail fast instead of waiting
question: Can a circuit breaker save the API when the database slows down?
description: The database slows down 50 times from 20 s to 40 s. The API has 100 slots and its calls to the database have a 300 ms timeout and a circuit breaker: after 5 consecutive failures, calls are rejected immediately for 5 s before one trial call is let through. Requests hit by the breaker still fail, but in milliseconds instead of after waiting.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each component has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the component is up.
Components do not know when their caller gave up; they finish the work and the answer is discarded.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: While the database is slow, most failures are circuit open, and they take milliseconds.
The database's queue stops overflowing, because the breaker stops sending calls while it is open.
After the database recovers, a trial call succeeds and the breaker closes again.
